owner_posts.post_text: A full diagnostic workup following twelve months of failed conception after miscarriage typically begins with AMH testing, a thyroid panel, pelvic ultrasound, and semen analysis covering both partners rather than assuming the cause lies with one. Accurate ovulation tracking through follicular monitoring or LH testing also informs the clinical picture. Dr. Mohit Saraogi, an IVF doctor in Mumbai, structures this evaluation as the standard first step for couples in this situation.

Lifestyle factors including smoking, excess alcohol, chronic stress, and inadequate sleep affect fertility in both men and women, compounding the impact of any underlying medical cause already present. None of these factors alone typically explains infertility, but their combined effect is measurable. As an infertility specialist in Mumbai, Dr. Mohit Saraogi addresses modifiable lifestyle factors alongside structured diagnostic testing during every fertility consultation.

Ovulation monitoring through blood tests and ultrasound scans ensures IUI is timed accurately to the fertile window, which directly affects the likelihood of successful fertilisation in a given cycle. This monitoring is conducted throughout both natural and medicated IUI protocols. Dr. Mohit Saraogi, providing IUI Treatment in Mumbai, builds this monitoring into every treatment cycle, adjusting timing based on each patient's individual ovulatory response rather than a fixed calendar schedule.

IVF healthcare is a coordinated clinical process — ovarian stimulation, egg retrieval under ultrasound guidance, laboratory fertilisation through IVF or ICSI, embryo culture to blastocyst stage, and timed uterine transfer — supported throughout by hormonal monitoring, diagnostic review, and personalised protocol adjustments. Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre, an IVF doctor in Mumbai, builds each treatment plan around individual diagnostic findings rather than a generalised fertility protocol.

Research across millions of IVF births shows no significant difference in the cognitive, physical, or psychological development of children conceived through IVF compared to those conceived naturally. Concerns about IVF babies' health persist largely because they are not consistently addressed at the consultation stage. Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre, where an IVF doctor in Mumbai, integrates clear, evidence-based health outcome discussions into every patient consultation before any cycle is recommended or initiated.

AMH reflects the quantity of remaining follicles in the ovaries, but its clinical significance depends entirely on the patient's age — a reading of 1.2 ng/mL means something very different at 29 than at 41. Normal reference ranges shift with age: 2.5–5.0 ng/mL at 25–30 years, narrowing to 0.5–2.5 ng/mL between 36 and 40. As an IVF specialist in Mumbai, Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre interprets AMH alongside antral follicle count and prior stimulation response before finalising any fertility treatment approach.

IUI involves processing a semen sample in the laboratory to concentrate motile sperm, then placing them directly into the uterus via a thin catheter timed to coincide with ovulation — eliminating the cervical barrier that filtered sperm must otherwise navigate in natural conception. The procedure takes under 10 minutes and requires no anaesthesia. Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre offers IUI Treatment in Mumbai with ovulation monitoring and a full diagnostic workup before any protocol is recommended.

PGT-A screens IVF embryos for chromosomal abnormalities before transfer — identifying which embryos have the correct chromosome count and reducing the risk of failed implantation and miscarriage in high-risk groups. It is most clinically relevant for women over 37, those with recurrent miscarriage, and patients with repeated implantation failure despite good-quality embryos. As an IVF specialist in Mumbai, Saraogi Hospital recommends PGT-A based on case history and failure pattern, not as a routine add-on.

No injection IVF — also referred to as natural or minimal stimulation IVF — relies on the body's own hormonal cycle to develop eggs, either without stimulation medications or with a significantly reduced oral medication protocol. It is suited to select patient profiles where conventional stimulation may not be the most appropriate path. An IVF doctor in Mumbai at Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre evaluates each patient's ovarian response and medical history before recommending this or any other fertility protocol.

AMH levels guide IVF planning but do not set a fixed cutoff for eligibility. A range of 1.0–3.5 ng/mL is considered optimal, yet cycles with AMH below 0.5 ng/mL can still proceed with adjusted stimulation protocols. Age and antral follicle count matter as much as AMH when assessing ovarian reserve. Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre and IVF specialist in Mumbai, individualises stimulation plans based on the full fertility profile, not a single marker.

Health discussions, especially around fertility and reproductive health, are often delayed because they feel confusing, uncomfortable, or overwhelming.

At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe empathy begins with making every health conversation feel simple, transparent, and easier to navigate.

Male fertility is often overlooked until the journey to parenthood takes longer than expected.

But fertility is not only about sperm count. Sperm quality, including movement and overall health, can also play an important role in conception.
Advanced techniques like Microfluidics help select healthier moving sperm during IVF treatment, supporting a more personalised approach to fertility care.
This Men's Health Month, let's encourage earlier conversations, timely evaluations, and greater awareness around male fertility health.

Some dreams take a little longer to come true.

This Father’s Day, we’re celebrating every dad who held on to hope, believed through the waiting, and never gave up on his dream of a family.

In IVF, precision matters at every stage.

From the collection of eggs and sperm to embryo transfer, accurate identification and verification play an important role throughout the treatment journey.

RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) technology adds an additional layer of electronic witnessing by assigning unique identifiers to biological samples and tracking them through key stages of the IVF process. This helps strengthen traceability and supports laboratory protocols designed to minimise the possibility of mix-ups.
At Nova IVF Fertility, RFID-based witnessing is integrated into our IVF laboratory processes as part of our commitment to maintaining high standards of safety and care.

A diagnosis of azoospermia can feel overwhelming, especially when a semen analysis shows no sperm. For many men, it may seem like the end of the road to fatherhood.

However, in some cases, sperm may still be present within the testes and can sometimes be retrieved through specialised procedures such as TESA, TESE or Micro-TESE. These retrieved sperm may then be used in IVF/ICSI treatment, offering some couples an opportunity to pursue pregnancy using their own sperm and eggs.
This Men’s Health Month, let’s remember that the right diagnosis and expert evaluation can make all the difference.

Father's Day: AI Now Reading Sperm, Giving Hope of Fatherhood to Infertile Men
Dr. PGL Lalit Kumar, Head of Embryology and Scientific Director, Nova IVF Fertility

The adoption of AI in fertility care is increasing, enhancing the precision and efficiency of evaluations.

This Men’s Health Month, it’s important to remember that a man’s health extends beyond just himself.

Physical health, emotional well-being, lifestyle habits, and reproductive health can all influence not only his own future, but also the well-being of his partner and the family he hopes to build.
Small everyday choices, timely health check-ups, and greater awareness can make a meaningful difference over time. Prioritising health today is also an investment in healthier tomorrows for the generations ahead.

At Nova IVF Fertility, we guide you towards simple, sustainable habits that work with your lifestyle, helping you move forward, one step at a time.

Around 15–20 eggs begin developing in your ovaries each month.

But the body naturally selects just one dominant egg and asks the rest to stop growing.
This is a normal biological process, not a limitation.
In IVF, this process is supported differently, allowing multiple eggs to continue developing for better chances of conception.
At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe awareness of your body helps you make more informed fertility choices.
